analysis: The PR changes only documentation: one table row in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (line 97) and one in docs/architecture/inference.md (gpt_oss row, ~line 1163). The hardware-support.md change adds a caveat that the gpt-oss-20b activation floor (3.5 GiB) was measured with float32 activations after layer 0 and has not been re-measured with bf16 activations. The inference.md change notes that a bf16 checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, citing GPTOSS+Experts.swift `swiglu`. No code, configuration, crypto, auth or attestation behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The prefix-cache threat T-041 (SSD tier, HMAC lookup, TTL, scoping) is untouched, and no security control is altered or weakened. Possible integration question: the companion code change (not in this batch) that makes gpt-oss activations bf16 could alter memory use. The documented floor is unverified for that case, which is an availability and memory-admission concern (T-016 and T-029 are loosely related). Admission is still enforced by per-request byte accounting, so this is not a demonstrable regression from the supplied docs. A reviewer of the code change should confirm the 3.5 GiB floor remains safe. Only the head side of the hardware-support.md excerpt (lines 458-503) and the base text of inference.md were supplied; the changed rows are covered via the patch excerpts. I found no security regression and nothing that invalidates the threat model.
